hypothesis: If the claim holds, a public account of living elephants says the trunk is a nostril, that the trunk brings food and water to the mouth, and that the trunk coils around or pulls up trees or stems.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered (claim supported). All three components are supported by at least one sentence in the combined text of the Animal Diversity Web accounts of Loxodonta africana and Elephas maximus and the ElephantVoices trunk-behavior pages linked from the ethogram index. Nostril: the sentence contains trunk or proboscis, and nostril, nose, or nasal. Food and drink: the sentence contains trunk or proboscis, mouth, and food, water, or drink. Trees: the sentence contains trunk or proboscis, and tree, stem, or branch, and coil, wrap, uproot, tear, or pull. A sentence split on period, exclamation mark or question mark is the unit.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. A component is refuted only by a sentence that contains the same content words and also says does not, cannot, or never. The claim is refuted if every component is refuted. It is mixed if at least one component is supported and at least one is refuted. A component with neither a support sentence nor a denial is untested. If any component is untested, the verdict is inconclusive with reason underpowered. If none of the three pages can be downloaded, the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable. A checksum mismatch on a re-download of a page, after the HTML processing-time or session token is left as-is only when the normalized text hash matches, is not by itself a failure; the normalized visible text is what is hashed.

test_contract.expected_observation: At least one sentence identifies the trunk as a nostril or nose, at least one says the trunk brings food or water to the mouth, and at least one says the trunk coils around, wraps, pulls, tears or uproots a tree, stem or branch.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: A sentence that denies one of those three acts or denies that the trunk is a nostril. Silence is not a denial.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Public natural-history accounts of living elephants (Elephantidae) that describe the trunk in prose. The accounts must not be Aristotle's text. Video that cannot be transcribed in this run does not count. Both living genera are in scope; one genus is enough to support an existence claim about elephants, and an explicit denial for both genera would be required to refute.
test_contract.inference_method: Split the visible text into sentences. Score each sentence with the keyword rules above. A component is supported by one matching sentence and refuted only by a denial. All three supported and none refuted yields supports. Any untested component yields inconclusive underpowered.

interpretation: The sentence says three things: the proboscis is a nostril, it is used as a hand to bring food and fluid to the mouth, and it tears up trees by coiling around their stems. 'As a hand' is read through those acts, not through a count of manipulative neurons. The test looks for the three acts in modern natural-history prose. It does not measure how often they occur.
confidence_rule_preregistered: All three components supported and none denied: 0.6. Mixed: 0.45. Inconclusive: 0.35. The ceiling is 0.6 because the data are prose accounts, not a counted sample of behavior.
caveats: Criteria were written before the account pages were downloaded. Only the HTTP status of the three landing URLs was checked.
Keyword sentences can match a negation that does not use the words does not, cannot or never. Any such sentence is quoted in the output so the match can be checked.
